# Horizon Entropy as Vacuum Entanglement

Jacobson’s vacuum-entanglement account develops the proposal that local horizon entropy is regulated entanglement across the horizon, an interpretation already suggested in his 1995 equation-of-state paper. The finite area density still enters as an assumption; the 2012 proposal that gravitational fluctuations themselves regulate the ultraviolet divergence is a physical heuristic rather than a demonstrated microscopic theory.

The primary source for the self-regulation argument is [[library/gravitation-and-vacuum-entanglement-entropy/inq|Jacobson 2012]]; its 1995 antecedent is [[library/thermodynamics-of-spacetime-the-einstein-equation-of-state/inq|archived here]].

## Conditional thermodynamic statement

The Minkowski vacuum restricted to a Rindler wedge is thermal with respect to the boost generator. In units \(c=k_B=1\), its dimensionful boost temperature is

$$
T_{\mathrm{boost}}=\frac{\hbar}{2\pi}.
$$

Suppose ultraviolet gravitational physics renders the vacuum entanglement across a causal horizon finite, with universal density \(\alpha\), and suppose its variation obeys

$$
\delta S=\frac{\delta Q}{T}
$$

on every local causal horizon. Then [[jacobson-local-horizon-thermodynamics]] yields Einstein gravity with

$$
G=\frac{1}{4\hbar\alpha},
\qquad
S_{\mathrm{BH}}=\frac{A}{4\hbar G}.
$$

The equation identifies the entropy density required by the observed gravitational coupling. It does not calculate that density from independent microscopic data.

## Gravitational cloaking heuristic

For a correlated pair separated by a proper distance \(\ell\), estimate

$$
E\sim\frac{\hbar}{\ell}.
$$

Its metric perturbation is of order

$$
\frac{GE}{\ell}
\sim
\frac{\ell_P^2}{\ell^2}.
$$

At \(\ell\lesssim\ell_P\), the causal geometry fluctuates strongly enough that a fixed smooth horizon can no longer sharply separate the pair. Jacobson proposes that this “cloaks” the trans-Planckian horizon-straddling correlations which would otherwise produce an unbounded entropy.

This is a scale argument. It does not construct the fluctuating geometry, a regulator-independent entropy, or a Hilbert-space factorization across a quantum horizon.

## Species and running coupling

For \(N\) matter species and a running Newton coupling, the proposed cutoff scale satisfies schematically

$$
\ell_c^2
=\hbar G(G_0,\ell_c,N),
$$

while the regulated entropy scales as

$$
S\sim\frac{NA}{\ell_c^2}.
$$

Recovering the Bekenstein–Hawking coefficient would require

$$
\frac{N}{\ell_c^2}
\sim
\frac{1}{\hbar G_0}.
$$

The paper presents this as a target, not a solved species problem. Strong coupling, nonminimal couplings, gauge contact terms, graviton contributions, and the boundary condition for the running of \(G\) remain unresolved.

## Higher-curvature limitation

An approximate local boost Killing field is ambiguous at relative order

$$
O\!\left(\frac{\ell^2}{L_{\mathrm{curv}}^2}\right).
$$

Planck-suppressed higher-curvature corrections can enter at the same order. Thus the local-horizon thermodynamic argument may be unable to distinguish the desired correction from the geometric “fuzz” in the approximate symmetry itself.

The controlled conclusion is narrow: vacuum entanglement is a plausible interpretation of the universal area density used by the Einstein equation-of-state argument. Gravitational self-regulation of that entropy remains an unfinished microscopic proposal.
